note: Add a new week by copying one block. The app reads this file from the live site, so no Apple update is needed.

questions.q: Rivets are set. What comes next before QC?
choices: Roll the truck out and let the sun finish it.
Post-heat edges and rivets so the film remembers the shape.
Pierce each rivet head so trapped air can escape.

questions.q: Swing doors, before any film. First step?
choices: Dry-fit the graphic with the doors shut.
Heat-set the door edges.
Open the doors and clean the hinge barrels and latch faces.

questions.q: A finished unit doesn't match the fleet card. Besides fixing it, what's the step?
choices: Log the deviation.
Change the card to match this unit.
Nothing, if it's close.

questions.q: Liner is piled on the floor where you're about to stage a big panel. Move?
choices: Clear the liner off the floor, then stage the panel with hinge tape.
Leave it. Clean up after the hang.
Stand on it. Keeps your boots off the concrete.

questions.q: Move on these finger rows?
choices: Squeegee them flat, hard.
Lift a finger and chase it out.

questions.q: Unit 5 is finished and unit 1 still hasn't been QC'd. Problem?
choices: No. QC the whole fleet at the end.
No. Unit 1 was just the sample.
Yes. QC unit 1 before you finish more units.

questions.q: Trailer nose graphic is still under transfer tape. When does heat come in?
choices: Before registering, to relax the film.
While it's still under the tape.
After you squeegee and pull the tape, and only per the film TDS.

questions.q: Who signs off before a fleet unit goes out?
choices: Whoever finished it.
Nobody, if the checklist looks good.
The lead.

questions.q: How deep does a half-moon relief go?
choices: All the way to the panel edge.
Skip it. A straight slash across the face works.
Only as deep as the bunch.

questions.q: The torch is on the floor. When does it come up?
choices: Now, to relax the salmon panel before it's registered.
After the nose panel is down, and only per the film TDS.

questions.q: Where does this blade stay?
choices: Back into the face to square it up.
On the edge, cutting the waste. Not back into the finished face.

questions.q: Multi-bay cubby run. What keeps every bay on the same line?
choices: Shared baselines marked on the returns and floors.
Eyeballing each bay as you go.
Trimming each bay to fit afterward.

questions.q: Long wood-grain wall and the boards start to stair-step. Fix?
choices: Stretch the next panel to catch the line.
Register each panel to the last one before you glass it. Sight the seam from the far end.
Heat the seam straight.

questions.q: Next move on this hatch?
choices: Glass the broad hatch, then feed up to the chrome. No bridge over the bar.
Stretch over the chrome bar now and trim later.

questions.q: Box truck side. Rivet rows are marked and the film is ready. What do you glass first?
choices: The flat field. Leave the rivet lines staged, not crushed.
The rivet rows, one head at a time, before the flat.
The whole rivet field in one long stretch.

questions.q: Next move on this RV side?
choices: Climb with the full sheet and stretch it on.
Move the ladder instead of overreaching. Hinge the panel, then glass it.

questions.q: What's wrong on this panel?
choices: Only the top is stuck. The rest of the field is wrinkled and loose.
Rivets are tented along a seam.

questions.q: Your IPA wipe beads up near a door seal. What's that telling you?
choices: Normal. The film will cover it.
Silicone. Resolve it before you hang.
The surface is too clean for the adhesive.

questions.q: Trailer rivet graphic is squeegeed, hinge tape still on. When do the rivets get post-heated?
choices: After the tape comes off and each rivet is set.
Now, while the tape holds everything.
Before the squeegee, to soften the rivets.

questions.q: Slider is wrapped. Film catches when the door runs. What went wrong?
choices: Gap and seal cuts weren't managed. Film is binding in the track.
Not enough heat on the field.
The door got cycled before post-heat.

questions.q: Pulling the liner on a big sheet. When do you squeegee?
choices: As you pull the liner.
After the whole liner is off.
Only once the sheet is trimmed.

questions.q: Next move in this box?
choices: Move the can, glass the sheet to the walls, then wrap or trim the bare plywood rim.
Leave the rim bare. It's inside the box.

questions.q: Walking the rivet row for QC. What are you looking for?
choices: Gloss level across the panel only.
Nothing. A set rivet can't lift later.
Tents, silvering, and dirty bases.

questions.q: What will read as a defect on this run under shop lights?
choices: The metal clips and black pads still on the faces.
The color change from magenta to red.

questions.q: Checking the band level across the slider. Door open or shut?
choices: Shut only.
Open only.
Both. Shut and open.

questions.q: Class C is wrapped. How do you walk it before release?
choices: Front, side, rear for stripe and panel continuity, plus a distance look at the tall sides.
Up close on the cab only.
Skip the walk if the hang went clean.

questions.q: Why check this satin hood in raking light?
choices: Satin can't take a relief cut.
Satin shows every finger. No gloss reflection hides them.

questions.q: Fix order at this marker light?
choices: Cut the light out first, then chase the fingers.
Lift the fingers, glass toward the housing, then cut the light out.

questions.q: What's wrong with this nose panel?
choices: It's glassed but the film is scorched.
It's hung, not glassed. The crown seam is open and the lower edge is loose.

questions.q: Why the felt edge on this printed film?
choices: It heats the film as it goes.
It keeps the printed grain from getting scratched.

questions.q: About to make post-heat passes on a trailer. Liner scraps are piled at the base. Move?
choices: Heat carefully around them.
Clear the liner piles first.
Kick them under the trailer.

questions.q: Graphic is seated. What's left before you call it done?
choices: Post-heat the whole graphic again to be safe.
Pull the nose tape low and slow, then check the rivet line and wheel-well edge.

questions.q: Film snags as you feed it into a cubby. Likely cause?
choices: It is bridging the opening. Feed the corners; do not bridge.
The cubby is too clean.
The squeegee has a felt edge.

questions.q: Liftgate with a deep plate pocket. What goes first?
choices: Feed the plate pocket, then the field.
Hang and glass the main rear field.
Trim the voids, then hang.

questions.q: The face is glassed. What still needs work?
choices: The raw plywood inside the round holes. Wrap or tuck each edge.
The QR code needs a relief cut.

questions.q: What's the rule on this peel?
choices: Pull straight up, fast.
Keep it low. Stop if the pink layer under it starts to lift.

questions.q: Plate recess isn't seated yet. Trim now?
choices: Yes. Trimming first makes the feed easier.
Yes, then heat the edge so it shrinks in.
No. Seat the recess first, then trim into the voids.

questions.q: How do you finish this inside corner?
choices: Stretch one sheet across the inside angle.
Glass each wall, then tuck the corner.

questions.q: Long trailer, before the first segment goes up. First step?
choices: Plan the segment map on paper or photos.
Hang the middle segment and work out.
Order one full-length sheet.

questions.q: Where does this knife stay?
choices: In the corner, off the show face, with the white wall as the guide.
Out on the show face for a straighter line.

questions.q: You're up on an RV roof and a forklift starts moving through the bay. Move?
choices: Keep working. The driver will go around.
Speed up and finish before it gets close.
Stop and coordinate around the bay traffic.

questions.q: Two crews keep waiting on the same tools. Fix?
choices: Stagger the crews so no vehicle is starved of tools.
Put both crews on one vehicle.
Skip the steps that need the missing tool.

questions.q: What has to happen before this blade touches the film?
choices: Clean off the drop and the specks.
Nothing. Cut right through them.

questions.q: Film is bunching at a rear-door hinge. When do the relief cuts go in?
choices: Early, to release the bunching.
After the film tears, to clean it up.
Never. Stretch through it.

questions.q: Tall box side. You're on the ladder and the panel edge is just out of reach. Fix?
choices: Lean out and grab it. It's one reach.
Step up on the top cap for the extra height.
Climb down and move the ladder.

questions.q: How do you inspect a fleet unit at QC?
choices: Distance view only.
Distance view, plus a close rivet and edge inspection.
Close up only.

questions.q: Bubbles in the corners of a soft-seated recess. What caused them?
choices: Not enough application fluid.
Air trapped in the corners. Chase it out toward the open edges.
Using a felt squeegee.

questions.q: How do you wrap these slats?
choices: One sheet stretched across all the openings.
Each slat on its own.

questions.q: Headlight pocket, film is seated. Next move?
choices: Cut flush on the lens face.
Fresh blade, cut into the gap, leave a small tuck behind the housing.
Score the paint so the cut tracks.

questions.q: Score marks on the hinge face after cutting. What went wrong?
choices: The film wasn't heated enough.
The blade was too fresh.
The blade crossed the paint instead of cutting into the void.

questions.q: A helper wants to spray a glide product so the squeegee slides easier. Answer?
choices: No. Nothing oily goes under the adhesive.
Fine on commercial sides.
Fine, if you heat harder after.

questions.q: Inside corner on an interior panel. Where does the relief cut go?
choices: Off the show face.
Dead center on the show face.
No relief. Stretch one sheet around.

questions.q: Cutting in the corner crease. Which way does the blade travel?
choices: Toward your body for control.
Away from your body.
Across the show face.

questions.q: Rear-door registration is confirmed. How does the liner come off?
choices: All at once to save time.
In sections, squeegeeing the field as you go.
Leave it on and heat through it.

questions.q: Architectural panel hang. First step?
choices: Knife-trim the reveals.
Seat the corners and returns.
Survey the panel layout and pattern direction.

questions.q: Tall graphic, field is glassed. What do you check before you commit the recesses?
choices: Nothing. Recesses come first anyway.
Level lines, from a distance.
Just the rivet heads, up close.

questions.q: What is standing against the orange panel at the door?
choices: A folding ladder, set right at the door.
A film roll on a stand.

questions.q: Knife is chewing the edge at an interior corner. Fix?
choices: Snap a fresh blade.
Press harder.
Heat the corner, then cut.

questions.q: Roof flats are glassed. How do you work the channels?
choices: Hard-card them flat in one stroke.
Feed them with soft tools.
Torch the film until it drops in.

questions.q: Where does the cut go on this door handle?
choices: Into the black voids, off the paint, leaving a tuck the housing can hide.
Straight across the face of the scoop.
